profile.summary: MixingDTA predicts drug-target affinity: given a drug SMILES string and a protein sequence, it returns a continuous affinity value. It does not learn its own sequence representations. Instead it takes embeddings from two pretrained language models, MolFormer for the molecule and ESM3-open for the protein, and feeds them to a trained aggregation network called MEETA. A data augmentation step called GBA-Mixup then builds extra training pairs by interpolating the embeddings of neighbouring drugs and proteins, which is aimed at sparse regions of affinity space and at unseen drugs or proteins.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract, Introduction, Figure 1 caption; README.md: Abstract

summary_quotes.text: In this work, we introduce MixingDTA, a novel framework to tackle data scarcity by incorporating domain-specific pretrained language models for molecules and proteins with our MEETA (MolFormer and ESM-based Efficient aggregation Transformer for Affinity) model.

We further address the label sparsity and cold-start challenges through a novel data augmentation strategy named GBA-Mixup, which interpolates embeddings of neighboring entities based on the guilt-by-association (GBA) principle, to improve prediction accuracy even in sparse regions of DTA space.
The embeddings corresponding to Drug SMILES and protein sequences are extracted from pretrained models.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: MEETA, the backbone, replaces the usual multi-head attention between drug and protein tokens with attention-free aggregation, which the authors say has linear rather than quadratic cost in sequence length and therefore lets them keep full drug and protein sequences instead of truncating them. The code implements this as a cross_AFT block with query, key and value projections in both directions, drug against protein and protein against drug, followed by a regression head that outputs a single value. The drug embeddings come from MolFormer-XL and the protein embeddings from ESM3-open with 1.4B parameters; everything in MEETA after those two encoders is trained. GBA-Mixup then samples a mixing ratio from a Beta distribution and interpolates the embeddings and labels of neighbouring drug-target pairs, where neighbours are defined by six perspectives. A meta-predictor finally combines the embeddings of the six encoders trained on those perspectives.

sections.title: Training and the six perspectives
sections.body: Training runs in two stages. In the first, the MEETA model is trained once for each of six cases, which the configuration file names none, all pair, drug, protein, drug and protein, and reversed, and which differ in how neighbouring pairs are connected and whether mixup is applied. In the second stage the six trained encoders are combined by a meta-predictor. The defaults in the configuration are 500 epochs, batch size 64, AdamW with a learning rate of 5e-5, an embedding width of 256 and five splits. The datasets are DAVIS, KIBA, BindingDB_Kd and PDBbind_Refined, the first three taken from TDC and shipped in the repository as pickle files already split for five-fold cross validation. The paper reports five-fold cross validation on DAVIS and KIBA with a train, validation and test ratio of 6:2:2, and full strings without truncation.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is no released set of MixingDTA weights. The README states that, because of storage limits, only the trained parameters for the DeepDTA version of MixingDTA are provided, on Google Drive, and the repository ships code for two backbones, MEETA and DeepDTA. A result should therefore name the backbone, the dataset, the case number or the integration stage, and the git commit, since all of those are command line or configuration choices. The maximum sequence length is a configuration value: 4200 by default, and the entry point raises it to 4700 together with other changes when the dataset is PDBbind_Refined.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised drug-target affinity regression framework built on two frozen pretrained language models, with a mixup style data augmentation step.

quotes.text: Drug–target affinity (DTA) prediction is an important regression task for drug discovery
MixingDTA framework consists of newly designed DTA architecture MEETA, augmented with our novel network-driven mixup technique GBA-Mixup.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: MEETA: MolFormer-XL drug embeddings and ESM3-open protein embeddings, joined by cross attention-free aggregation blocks with an embedding width of 256 in the default configuration, then a fully connected regression head. Six such encoders, one per GBA-Mixup perspective, are combined by a meta-predictor.

quotes.text: It employs cross-AFA (attention-free aggregation) to efficiently aggregate representations.

Multiview integration combines embeddings from six GBA-Mixup–trained encoders, each capturing a different neighborhood perspective. These integrated embeddings are fed into the meta-predictor’s fully connected layers for final binding-affinity prediction.

strengths.text: The augmentation step is separate from the backbone. The authors report that GBA-Mixup is model agnostic and gave gains across every backbone they tested, and the repository includes a DeepDTA backbone alongside MEETA to show this. The size of those gains is the authors' own claim.

quotes.text: Importantly, GBA-Mixup is model-agnostic, delivering performance gains across all tested backbone models of up to 16.9%.

run_guide.summary: Extract the two sets of language model embeddings, train the MEETA backbone once per perspective, then train the meta-predictor that integrates them.
prerequisites: The environment the README gives: conda with python 3.10, transformers, biopython, pytorch 2.3.1 with pytorch-cuda 12.1, esm, ipykernel, PyTDC 1.0.7, easydict, lifelines 0.29.0, scikit-learn 1.2.2 and rdkit 2023.9.6.
A GPU. Every training command takes a GPU device number.
Access to the ESM3 open small weights, which the README says are under the Cambrian non-commercial licence, and to MolFormer.
No licence is declared for the repository code, which the README says is for academic purposes.

notes: The record comes from the Wang and Cheng 2026 leakage-controlled benchmark preprint, which is on bioRxiv only (pdf at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.17.752433v1.full.pdf) and was not fetched in this pass, so nothing here is taken from it; Europe PMC shows no PMC copy of it. The record description calls MixingDTA a meta-ensemble using MolFormer and ESM3 features, which matches the sources; the exact wording used here follows the paper. The repository holds no licence file, so store_bytes is false for its files.
